text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Finnish newspapers this morning.
- Critics say Bank of Finland, through intervention, is effectively devaluing the markka in midst of economic upswing.
- Fierce competition and small scale of Finnish food market has kept international industry giants from conquering Finland as was expected after it joined the European Union in 1995.
- Heavy snowfall in Helsinki puts pressure on ploughing vehicles -- big piles of snow have shoved onto side streets, burying pavements, hindering traffic and blocking parking lots.
- Talks on wood purchase prices may prove difficult -- forest industry expects discounts but forest owners are seeking price hikes, industry says.

- The leading Finnish banks Merita, OKOBANK and Postipankki have saved 200 million markka, twice expected amount, by bundling their cashpoint machine operations into Automatia Oy, Automatia managing director says.
- Passenger ferry operator Silja Oy to lay off 135 in April following the sale of its Silja Scandinavia vessel to rival Viking Line.

- Stolen 18th-century Guarnerius violin valued at 500,000 markka was found in black plastic bag after pleas from the owner to the thief not to harm and return the instrument, which was too well known to be sold on the black market anyway.
- Wealthy Russians are getting bored of Helsinki shopping and turning their eyes to Berlin, Paris, Rome and New York where they can buy the latest fashion items long before they reach Helsinki.
- Chairman of the Finnish Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK) Esa Swanljung says a new wage agreement may meet opposition among many unions.
- Norwegian shipyard Kvaerner Kleven AS makes no bid to build a new Finnish multi-purpose ice-breaker which would mean it would be built in Finland.
- Local Tampere telephone operator interested in bidding for Turun Puhelin, Turku telephone company, which the city of Turku is negotiating to sell to Swedish Telia.
